claims.text: Ni20Mn20Ga20Gd20Co20 is a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
The alloy is initially multiphase, with mixed gamma phase and martensite, prior to field-assisted processing.
Hot-magnetic drawing can be performed with an approximately 0.5 T external magnetic field applied during deformation.
Applying a 0.5 T field during hot-magnetic drawing changes Ni20Mn20Ga20Gd20Co20 from a multiphase gamma-plus-martensite structure to a single-phase L10-type twin martensite structure.
The applied magnetic field enhances the formation of twin martensite variants and twin boundaries relative to processing without a field.
The field biases the martensitic phase transformation toward a single-phase twin martensite structure.
The resulting twin martensite has high magnetic anisotropy.
Twin boundaries in the martensite act as effective pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
The field-induced twin boundaries impede domain-wall motion more effectively than the microstructure produced without a field.
More effective domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field.
Hot drawing under a 0.5 T field will produce higher coercivity than otherwise identical hot drawing without an applied field.
The intervention should operate at elevated thermomechanical-processing temperatures where martensitic transformation is accessible.
The coercivity effect should be most pronounced in high-entropy alloys capable of martensitic transformation with twin formation.
Alloys lacking martensitic transformation potential or sufficient magnetic anisotropy may not exhibit an increase in coercivity.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase and the optimal processing-field strength are not yet quantified.
Coercivity can be compared between field-processed and zero-field controls using hysteresis-loop magnetometry.
TEM or EBSD can be used to compare twin-martensite presence and density between the field-processed and control samples.
Failure to observe a statistically significant coercivity increase or enhanced twin-martensite formation in the field-processed samples would falsify the hypothesis.
